chapterNote: Solomon's psalm of the built house and the full quiver — the builder of the temple writing that building is God's work or it is nothing. Three vanities open it, the same shav that Ecclesiastes made famous: the house built without the LORD, the city guarded without the LORD, and the anxious grind of early rising and late sitting, eating the bread of painful toil — all empty, for He gives to His beloved even in their sleep. What anxiety cannot wring from a day, God grants to a resting heir. Then the psalm turns from houses of stone to the house of a family, and issues Scripture's great charter of children: not accidents, not burdens, not projects — a heritage from the LORD, the fruit of the womb His own reward. Sons and daughters of one's youth are arrows in a warrior's hand: made to be aimed and sent, reaching further than their father ever will. Blessed is the man whose quiver is full; when he stands at the gate, where courts convened and adversaries pressed their claims, he does not stand alone or ashamed. A psalm for builders, watchmen, workers, and above all for fathers — Adam's own banner over family life.

1.text: A song of ascents, of Solomon. Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor over it in vain; unless the LORD guards the city, the watchman stays awake for nothing.
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth] for Solomon [Shelomoh]. Except the LORD [YHWH] build [banah] the house [bayith], they labour [amal] in vain [shav — emptiness] that build it: except the LORD keep [shamar] the city [ir], the watchman [shomer] wakes [shaqad] but in vain [shav].
1.notes: From Shelomoh (H8010), who built the temple and knew which Builder mattered (cf. 1 Kings 8:27). The two great male labors, banah and shamar (H1129, H8104) — constructing and guarding — both come to shav (H7723), the empty nothing, without the LORD in the first clause. Effort is not the variable; blessing is.

2.text: It is useless for you to rise early and sit up late, eating the bread of anxious toil — for He gives to His beloved even in their sleep.
2.amp: It is vain [shav] for you to rise up [qum] early [shakam], to sit up [yashab] late [achar], to eat [akal] the bread [lechem] of sorrows [etsev — painful toil]: for so He gives [natan] His beloved [yadid] sleep [shena].
2.notes: The third shav is the grind itself: shakam and achar (H7925, H309), the day stretched at both ends, seasoned with etsev (H6089), the pain-word of the curse on work (cf. Genesis 3:17). The counterpoint is one of Scripture's gentlest lines: to His yadid (H3039), His beloved, He natan (H5414) gives — even while they sleep. Rest as an act of faith in the Giver.

3.text: Look — children are a heritage from the LORD; the fruit of the womb is a reward from Him.
3.amp: Lo, children [ben] are an heritage [nachalah — an inheritance, an estate] of the LORD [YHWH]: and the fruit [peri] of the womb [beten] is His reward [sakar — wages given].
3.notes: The psalm's hinge from stone houses to living ones. nachalah (H5159) is the land-inheritance word: children as the estate God deeds to a man. sakar (H7939) is wages — but given, not earned; every peri beten (H990) arrives as payment from a generosity that owed nothing (cf. Genesis 33:5).

4.text: Like arrows in the hand of a mighty warrior, so are the children of one's youth.
4.amp: As arrows [chets] are in the hand [yad] of a mighty man [gibbor — a warrior]; so are children [ben] of the youth [neurim].
4.notes: chets (H2671) in a gibbor's (H1368) hand: an arrow is shaped, straightened, aimed, and then RELEASED — it strikes where the archer cannot walk. Children of the neurim (H5271), of one's vigorous years, have time to be fletched well; they are a father's reach into a future he will not see.

5.text: Oh the blessedness of the man who has filled his quiver with them! They will not be put to shame when they speak with enemies in the gate.
5.amp: Happy [esher — oh the blessedness] is the man [geber] that has his quiver [ashpah] full [male] of them: they shall not be ashamed [bosh], but they shall speak [dabar — 'subdue, destroy', the KJV margin] with the enemies [oyeb] in the gate [shaar].
5.notes: The esher (H835) beatitude lands on the full ashpah (H827): abundance of children as armament, not encumbrance. The shaar (H8179) was courtroom and council; a geber (H1397) flanked by grown sons stands there unashamed, his case backed by the very heritage the LORD paid him. The psalm that began with builders ends with a house that speaks for itself.
